mechanism_narrative: The level of FEDFUNDS is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: lower FEDFUNDS predicts positive returns over the next 20 trading days due to compressed discount rates on equity cash flows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 6.5%, it predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to economic uncertainty and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 6.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) are both above their 3-month moving averages, it predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to synchronized demand and supply expansion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where both HOUST and INDPRO are above their 3-month moving averages, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 0.5% over the past 3 months), S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 20 trading days due to increased discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and rising for 3 months, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of industrial production (INDPRO) is positively related to S&P 500 forward returns: higher INDPRO predicts positive returns over the next 60 trading days due to stronger economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO > 100, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 260.5, it predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to heightened inflation fears.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 260.5, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) are both above their 3-month moving averages, it predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to improving labor market and housing conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where both PAYEMS and HOUST are above their 3-month moving averages, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (defined by UNRATE exceeding 6.5% and rising for 3 months), S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 5 trading days due to economic distress and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 6.5% and rising for 3 months, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
